content.title: WHY YOUR 'HEALTHY' MEALS AREN'T ACTUALLY WORKING FOR YOU
facts: **Boiling broccoli** – This drains most of its vitamin C and antioxidants straight into the water; steam it for 5 minutes instead to keep nutrients intact.
**Salad first** – Eating raw vegetables before any fat or protein means less absorption of vitamins A, E, and K, since they're fat-soluble and need oil to be absorbed.
**Rinsing canned beans** – Skipping this step leaves excess sodium on the beans; a quick 30-second rinse cuts the sodium content significantly.
**Microwaving in plastic** – Even 'microwave-safe' containers can leach chemicals into food when heated; transfer to glass or ceramic first.
**Overcooking eggs** – Yolks cooked too long at high heat lose more of their choline and healthy fats; soft-scrambled or poached preserves more.
**Adding oil too early** – Pouring olive oil into a hot pan before sautéing breaks it down and creates harmful compounds; add it after the pan has cooled slightly or at the end.
**Skipping the resting time** – Cutting grilled chicken or meat immediately releases most of the juices and nutrients onto the cutting board; wait 5-10 minutes first.
**Overwashing mushrooms** – Soaking them in water makes them absorb liquid like a sponge, diluting flavor and nutrients; wipe with a damp cloth instead.

content.caption:
A few of these mistakes are more sneaky than people realize. Take broccoli — the vitamin C in it is water-soluble, meaning it literally dissolves and leaches out the moment it hits boiling water, so steaming preserves far more of it. Then there's the salad-first habit: your body needs dietary fat present in the digestive tract to actually absorb vitamins A, E, D, and K from those leafy greens, so a salad with zero dressing or protein is doing a lot less for you than it seems. And with canned beans, that starchy liquid they sit in (sometimes called aquafaba) carries a surprising amount of added sodium that a quick rinse under the tap washes right off. Everyone's kitchen habits are a little different, so start with the one that feels easiest to fix first.
